title: Validation & Intervention Testing for Aging, Longevity and Healthspan
official: Validation & Intervention Testing for Aging, Longevity and Healthspan (VITAL-H)
summary:
The study aims to address the gap between lifespan and healthspan (years of life free of age-related diseases and disabilities) by testing whether 2 approved U.S Food and Drug Administration (FDA) medications, dapagliflozin and semaglutide, can help people stay healthier as they age and delay the age-related functional decline. The study will test these medications over 36 months of treatment plus 6 months of observational follow up to see if they can safely maintain health and function during aging and eventually support their use for extending healthspan.

This study is being done because there are limited ways to slow down the age-related health and functional decline, and few reliable ways to measure early changes in healthspan in humans. The 2 study drugs have shown promising results in laboratory and early human studies, but more evidence is needed.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.
2. Males and females; Age 60-75
3. Willingness to adhere to the study intervention regimen (dapagliflozin or semaglutide).
4. Body mass index 20-40 kg/m2
5. Community dwelling

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Any medical condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would place the participant at increased risk for participation.
2. Participation in another treatment or intervention study within 6 months
3. Use of the following medication or supplements

   * That may be used for weight or appetite control
   * That may be used for glucose lowering
   * Immunosuppressant or biologics
4. Any of the following conditions

   * Myocardial infarction (MI), cerebrovascular accident (CVA/stroke), congestive heart failure (CHF) or revascularization procedures like percutaneous coronary intervention (stents)
   * Renal impairment with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR\<45)
   * Requirement of assistive devices for ambulation
   * Pancreatitis history (if cause has been removed then okay to enroll)
   * Recurrent urinary tract infections (2 or more within 6 months, or 3 or more within past 12 months)
   * Personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2
   * Active cancer (okay if in remission for ≥ 3 years or had non melanoma skin cancer)
   * Uncontrolled Hypertension above 160/90 (we will include individuals with controlled hypertension and no complications)
   * Diabetes or Hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5%
   * Multiple sclerosis, MS, Parkinson Disease, mild cognitive impairment, dementia
   * History of solid organ transplant
5. Planned elective orthopedic surgery during the study
6. Hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs
7. Prisoner
8. Females who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant
